---

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**This is the shape of the first intermediate**: 15 questions, 2 points each, 30 in total; 6 multiple choice, 3 true/false, 6 open questions answered with R code, the numbers and one sentence that reads them. 60 minutes. Open questions are marked 0 to 2 in steps of 0.5: the sentence that reads the numbers is what separates 1.5 from 2. The intermediate has different questions on the same topics.
:::

Data: `mtcars`, `cars`, `PlantGrowth`, `warpbreaks` and `lung` ship with R (`library(survival)` for `lung`); [`churn.csv`](../materials/churn.csv) is the course dataset. Work in RStudio with the script of the lab open: every function needed is in it. Check yourself against the [solutions](m1-practice-solutions.qmd) only after writing your own sentence.


## A · Multiple choice

One option is right.

### 1

In R, after model1 <- lm(y ~ x), the command abline(model1):

a. tests H0: b = 0
b. draws the fitted line on the scatter plot
c. prints the residuals
d. standardises x

### 2

In baltimore, lm(PRICE ~ AGE + AC) gives intercept 44.8, AGE -0.17 and AC 19.7 (AC = 1 if the house has air conditioning). The predicted price of a 10-year-old house with air conditioning is:

a. 44.8 - 0.17 * 10 + 19.7 = 62.8
b. 44.8 + 19.7 = 64.5
c. 19.7 * 10 = 197
d. 44.8 - 0.17 * 10 = 43.1

### 3

The degrees of freedom of a regression are:

a. R-squared times n
b. always n - 1
c. the number of predictors
d. the number of observations minus the number of parameters, n - p

### 4

In the BrainCancer Cox model the coefficient of the Karnofsky index ki is negative and significant. This means:

a. the survival curve rises with time
b. a higher Karnofsky index raises the probability of death
c. a higher Karnofsky index lowers the hazard: patients in better condition die later
d. the baseline hazard is negative

### 5

vif(model) returns 1.33 for both predictors. According to the rule seen in the lecture:

a. the model is refitted without the intercept
b. both variables are retained: the threshold is VIF > 10 (tolerance < 0.1)
c. both variables are discarded
d. the one with the higher VIF is discarded first

### 6

Two models are compared: M1: Y ~ X1 and M2: Y ~ X1 + X2. For X2 the p-value is 0.002; training RMSE 5.12 (M1) vs 5.05 (M2); cross-validated RMSE 5.30 (M1) vs 5.29 (M2). The reading is:

a. X2 improves prediction substantially, since the p-value is small
b. X2 is statistically significant, but the predictive improvement is negligible
c. M2 overfits, because its training RMSE is lower
d. the two RMSEs contradict the p-value, so one of the computations is wrong

## B · True or false

Say which, and why, in one line.

### 7

Leave-one-out cross-validation is K-fold cross-validation with K equal to the number of observations.

### 8

The R-squared of a logistic regression is read like the R-squared of a linear regression.

### 9

In a two-tailed test (H1: mu different from mu0) the rejection region is split between the two tails of the sampling distribution, alpha/2 on each side.

## C · Open questions

Code, result, one sentence. The sentence is the part that is marked.

### 10

On churn.csv, fit churn ~ tenure_months + contract + monthly_charge (logistic). A new customer has been with us 3 months, is on a month-to-month contract and pays 90 euros a month: what is the probability that they churn? And the same customer on a two-year contract after 36 months? Code, numbers, sentence.

### 11

On churn.csv, fit churn ~ tenure_months + contract + monthly_charge (logistic). Build the classification table at the 0.5 threshold and compute the percentage of correctly classified customers. Is it a good model? Compare with the naive rule 'nobody churns'.

### 12

On mtcars, with set.seed(1), split the cars 70/30 into train and test (hold-out), as in the lab. Fit mpg ~ wt on train and compute the RMSE on train and on test; then fit mpg ~ wt + hp and do the same. (a) Report the four RMSEs. (b) Does hp improve prediction? Why is the test RMSE the number to compare, and what is the weakness of a single split here?

### 13

lung: 228 patients, time in days, status (2 = died). Fit the Kaplan-Meier curve of the whole sample. (a) Report the median survival with its 95% interval. (b) Report the probability of surviving one year (365 days) with its interval, from summary(fit, times = 365). (c) Why is the raw share of patients with time > 365, 28.5%, the wrong number?

### 14

PlantGrowth: the dried weight of 30 plants under a control and two treatments. Does the treatment matter, and if so WHICH treatments differ from which? Code, result, one sentence.

### 15

On mtcars, compare mpg ~ wt and mpg ~ wt + hp with 5-fold cross-validation, set.seed(123), using the SAME folds for both. Report the two cross-validated RMSE. Does hp improve prediction, and does the answer agree with its p-value?
